P08-002.boundary_rationale: Onset: the sub-onset 'son of man' at Ezek.33.10 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם אֱמֹר֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֵּ֤ן אֲמַרְתֶּם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי פְשָׁעֵ֥ינוּ וְחַטֹּאתֵ֖ינוּ עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּבָ֛ם אֲנַ֥חְנוּ נְמַקִּ֖ים וְאֵ֥יךְ נִֽחְיֶֽה (oshb:Ezek.33.10) opens with the quoted popular saying it will refute, immediately following the samekh-marked close at oshb:Ezek.33.9. That re-address turns the speech from the prophet-directed watchman charge back to the people and is licensed as an onset, while the far face behind it carries that samekh and no formula, a mark only. An oath-plus-utterance combination follows at Ezek.33.11 אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם חַי אָ֣נִי נְאֻ֣ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה אִם אֶחְפֹּץ֙ בְּמ֣וֹת הָרָשָׁ֔ע כִּ֣י אִם בְּשׁ֥וּב רָשָׁ֛ע מִדַּרְכּ֖וֹ וְחָיָ֑ה שׁ֣וּבוּ שׁ֜וּבוּ מִדַּרְכֵיכֶ֧ם הָרָעִ֛ים וְלָ֥מָּה תָמ֖וּתוּ בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.33.11), carrying its own pe mark; this is disclosed as close-grade material that is NOT final here, because the same disputation continues through a second 'son of man' sub-onset at Ezek.33.12 restating the principle for “the children of your people” (web:Ezek.33.12) and on through the righteous/wicked case-pairs of 33.14-19. Close: a second pe mark follows Ezek.33.20 וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י אִ֧ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֛יו אֶשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶתְכֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל (oshb:Ezek.33.20), which restates the people's complaint verbatim against 33.17 -- the four pointed words לֹ֥א יִתָּכֵ֖ן דֶּ֣רֶךְ אֲדֹנָ֑י stand byte-identical in both verses (oshb:Ezek.33.17, oshb:Ezek.33.20; WLC/OSHB, single witness) -- and then adds YHWH's verdict (“I will judge every one of you after his ways” (web:Ezek.33.20)), which stands at 33.20 only and has no counterpart anywhere in 33.17, marking the disputation's true end. That near face is a verdict clause with no formula of its own -- the discourse close of the disputation, corroborated by the pe that follows and by no formula -- while the far face past it opens the next unit on the dateline at 33:21. A close seam whose near face is a discourse close without a formula is what this row's medium_low records, whatever stands on its far face. MT 33.20 carries no sof-pasuq in this witness — it stands instead with an untyped OSHB editorial note, 'We read punctuation in L differently from BHS,' immediately before the pe. The section-mark witness records that this verse carries no sof pasuq; the editors' note stands in its place. This is disclosed as a single-witness punctuation divergence; no boundary is argued from the absent mark, only from the pe that follows and the topical restatement it closes.
P08-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: The rival onset is the 'and you, son of man' (ve'attah) at Ezek.33.12, and the address there does shift from בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל at 33.10 to בְּנֵֽי עַמְּךָ֙ at 33.12 (oshb:Ezek.33.10, oshb:Ezek.33.12; WLC/OSHB, single witness). The two are titles for one audience inside one speech: the house-of-Israel title stands at 33.10, 33.11 and 33.20, the children-of-your-people title at 33:2, 33.12 and 33.17, and the chapter's own address opens at 33:2 with the second of them, so the shift is a title shift inside one addressee group and not an addressee change, and on that ground the ve'attah is not licensed here. The pe recorded on 33.11 is disclosed for the rival as a paragraph mark. Independently, cutting there would leave 33:10-11 as a two-verse row that is not a complete word-event unit, and 33:11's own close-shaped cluster cannot supply the missing onset -- its utterance formula stands mid-verse, at word 5 of that verse's 25, counting from the first, with independent imperatives running on after it, so 33.11 is not a close the rival could stand on, and a mark alone never carries that weight however strong the pe looks. The rival is therefore paragraph-grade, and the disputation runs on as one 'you say ... but I say' unit across 33:10-20, which is the near face on both of this row's seams.
P08-002.device_notes: unit_type disputation_oracle fits 33.10-20 as one unit; no category deviation. Row runs 11 verses, above the 7-10 typical band, held at medium_low rather than split: the rival onset is the ve'attah at 33.12, paragraph-grade and not licensed, since the address shifts only between two titles for one audience, and a cut there would in any case leave 33:10-11, under three verses and not a complete word-event unit. K/Q disclosure (single-witness): oshb:Ezek.33.13 carries one note, ketiv צדקתו / qere צִדְקֹתָיו֙, and oshb:Ezek.33.16 carries one note, ketiv חטאתו / qere חַטֹּאתָיו֙; each ketiv stands unpointed in the running text of this witness, each of the two notes carries two morpheme separators in the K/Q layer which are dropped from the forms as given here, and no boundary is argued from either Qere. The section-mark witness carries one K-Q pair at each of these two verses. Paseq (count-only, single-witness): Ezek.33.11 carries 2 occurrences; intra-verse position is unsourceable from the extract.

P08-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: MT 33:20 is followed by a pe (single-witness), corroborating the onset at 33:21; that pe stands where this witness records no sof pasuq on MT 33:20, and it is the only corroboration the onset carries from behind. The dateline at Ezek.33.21 וַיְהִ֞י בִּשְׁתֵּ֧י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֗ה בָּעֲשִׂרִ֛י בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֥ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לְגָלוּתֵ֑נוּ בָּא אֵלַ֨י הַפָּלִ֧יט מִירוּשָׁלִַ֛ם לֵאמֹ֖ר הֻכְּתָ֥ה הָעִֽיר (oshb:Ezek.33.21) — one of the book's 14 year-bearing oracle datelines and a hard seam — reports the fugitive's arrival with news the city has fallen. Ezek.33.22 וְיַד יְהוָה֩ הָיְתָ֨ה אֵלַ֜י בָּעֶ֗רֶב לִפְנֵי֙ בּ֣וֹא הַפָּלִ֔יט וַיִּפְתַּ֣ח אֶת פִּ֔י עַד בּ֥וֹא אֵלַ֖י בַּבֹּ֑קֶר וַיִּפָּ֣תַח פִּ֔י וְלֹ֥א נֶאֱלַ֖מְתִּי עֽוֹד (oshb:Ezek.33.22) follows with the hand-of-YHWH idiom (matched on the construct alone, one of 7 verses carrying the construct) and the mouth-opening event that fulfils the muteness first commissioned in ch. 3 and anticipated as a coming sign earlier in the book. This hand-of-YHWH occurrence opens no vision here — it is narrative notice, not a scene-transport marker. Close: a pe mark follows Ezek.33.22 (single-witness), and the verse completes the narrative beat before Ezek.33.23 opens a fresh, formally distinct word-event oracle. The onset's near face is licensed -- the dateline itself -- while the far face behind it carries that mark and no formula; the close's near face is 33:22's hand-of-YHWH and mouth-opening, a hard seam, and its far face is 33:23's fresh word-event formula. A licensed near face against a mark-only far face is what this row's medium records.
P08-003.device_notes: unit_type is a disclosed per-bytes deviation: classified commission_narrative (the muteness/mouth-opening device) rather than vision_report, because the hand-of-YHWH here is followed by narrative notice (the mouth-opening at Ezek.33.22) rather than any scene-transport or vision-inaugurating formula, and rather than disputation_oracle or judgment_oracle because the verses are narrative notice, not oracle speech. Under-3-verse row, disclosed as a two-verse unit bounded by 33:21's own dateline onset and the pe after 33:22.

P09-009.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.39.17 opens וְאַתָּ֨ה בֶן אָדָ֜ם כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהֹוִ֗ה אֱמֹר֩ לְצִפּ֨וֹר כָּל כָּנָ֜ף וּלְכֹ֣ל חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֗ה הִקָּבְצ֤וּ וָבֹ֨אוּ֙ הֵאָסְפ֣וּ מִסָּבִ֔יב עַל זִבְחִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר אֲנִ֜י זֹבֵ֤חַ לָכֶם֙ זֶ֣בַח גָּד֔וֹל עַ֖ל הָרֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַאֲכַלְתֶּ֥ם בָּשָׂ֖ר וּשְׁתִ֥יתֶם דָּֽם, combining the same ‘and you, son of man’ sub-onset class as 39.1 (and 36.1 earlier in the parent) with a messenger formula addressed this time to birds and beasts rather than to Gog -- a real addressee shift even though, like 39.1, it carries no word-event formula of its own and remains under 38.1's governing word-event frame. Close: the utterance formula closes 39.17-20 at oshb:Ezek.39.20 וּשְׂבַעְתֶּ֤ם עַל שֻׁלְחָנִי֙ ס֣וּס וָרֶ֔כֶב גִּבּ֖וֹר וְכָל אִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֑ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה, one of 81 such closes book-wide, with 39.21 then returning the address to the nations (“I will set my glory among the nations” (web:Ezek.39.21)) on a topical turn that carries no formula and no mark of its own, weighed from the far side.
P09-009.device_notes: 39.17 carries two paseq occurrences on the one verse (count-only, single-witness); no K/Q or editorial note falls in this span. The onset is a sub-onset licensed by the addressee change at 39.17, from Gog to the birds and the beasts of the field, and the row is held at medium because the seam behind it carries a mark and no formula. Onset corroboration: one samekh stands after MT 39:16 in this witness, single witness.

P09-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: a messenger formula reopens at oshb:Ezek.39.25 לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה עַתָּ֗ה אָשִׁיב֙ אֶת שבית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וְרִֽחַמְתִּ֖י כָּל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְקִנֵּאתִ֖י לְשֵׁ֥ם קָדְשִֽׁי on the word ‘therefore,’ immediately turning from the exile retrospective to the restoration promise. That turn addresses the same hearers as the retrospective before it, so it is a discourse turn and not a licensed sub-onset, and the far face behind it, oshb:Ezek.39.24, carries a samekh and no close-role formula -- its hidden-face clause is not a close device -- so the onset seam is corroborated by a mark alone. In 39.25 the ketiv reads שבית (oshb:Ezek.39.25, ketiv) and the qere reads שְׁב֣וּת (oshb:Ezek.39.25, Qere) (a single-witness textual-variant site, disclosed, never argued as a boundary). Close: 39.25-29 ends at oshb:Ezek.39.29 וְלֹֽא אַסְתִּ֥יר ע֛וֹד פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶ֑ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר שָׁפַ֤כְתִּי אֶת רוּחִי֙ עַל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה, the standard utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature (one of 81 book-wide) with a pe mark recorded immediately after -- the close evidence the restoration collection's own boundary is anchored on, matching the point where the following material opens on a dateline plus hand-of-YHWH and transport at Ezek.40.1. The close seam stands top grade on both faces -- 39.29's utterance signature with the pe recorded after it, and the dateline with hand-of-YHWH and transport at 40.1 past it -- while the onset seam does not, and that is what this row's medium records.
P09-011.device_notes: No paseq falls in this span. 39.25 is a single-note K/Q verse (written שבית (oshb:Ezek.39.25, ketiv), read שְׁב֣וּת (oshb:Ezek.39.25, Qere)); no editorial note falls here. The span closes at 39.29, the restoration collection's own close; no material past 39.29 is claimed. The strict recognition formula stands at 39:28, interior to the span and not its close. The hidden-face clause that ends 39.24 recurs, negated, at 39.29, straddling this row's onset seam; it is continuity texture across the seam, not counterevidence against it.

P07-008.boundary_rationale: Onset side: the hard-seam dateline at oshb:Ezek.32.17 (year 12, day 15, with no month named in the verse -- 32:1 carries the twelfth month and this dateline carries none; perfect hayah word-event form) opens onto the son-of-man command at oshb:Ezek.32.18 to “wail for the multitude of Egypt” (web:Ezek.32.18) -- a different technical verb from the qinah noun that opened and closed 32:1-16, disclosed as a genre question rather than assumed continuous with it. Close side: the row runs through the taunt (32:19-21) and the protected, never-cut roster of fallen nations in Sheol (32:22-30) to the doubled utterance-formula close at oshb:Ezek.32.31 and oshb:Ezek.32.32, corroborated by a following pe, at the book's own P6 parent-collection close. The genre call (oracle_against_nation vs. lament_qinah) is held, not resolved; it does not bear on the seam grade. Both seams are two-faced and top grade: 32:16 ends on the utterance signature, verse-final, and carries a pe, against 32:17's dateline and hayah-form word-event; and 32:32 ends on the utterance signature, verse-final, with a pe after it, against the strict word-event formula at 33:1. Inside the span 32:31 ends on the utterance formula while 32:32 opens on כִּֽי (oshb:Ezek.32.32; WLC/OSHB, single witness) with no onset-class device, so that recurrence is paragraph-grade and not a rival; 32:18's son-of-man address corroborates the onset rather than opening a unit of its own; and the roster at 32:22-30 is never cut. No licensed or two-faced rival stands anywhere in the span, and its 16 verses are the Sheol roster entire, so the length is no ground against it. That is what this row's high grade records.

P08-012.boundary_rationale: Onset: a samekh follows MT 36:15 (single-witness), the paragraph mark behind this unit's onset. A fresh strict-form word-event formula crosses a hard seam at Ezek.36.16 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.36.16), the fifth such hard seam since Ezek.33.1 (33.1, 33.23, 34.1, 35.1, 36.16), and not the last: 37.15 and 38.1 follow. 'Son of man' at Ezek.36.17 בֶּן אָדָ֗ם בֵּ֤ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ יֹשְׁבִ֣ים עַל אַדְמָתָ֔ם וַיְטַמְּא֣וּ אוֹתָ֔הּ בְּדַרְכָּ֖ם וּבַעֲלִֽילוֹתָ֑ם כְּטֻמְאַת֙ הַנִּדָּ֔ה הָיְתָ֥ה דַרְכָּ֖ם לְפָנָֽי (oshb:Ezek.36.17) opens a retrospective on Israel's own defilement of the land and the resulting exile — a distinct tense and topic from the 'mountains of Israel' address just closed. Inside the span a samekh follows MT 36:21 (single-witness); the unit does not cut there because the messenger-formula pivot at Ezek.36.22 לָכֵ֞ן אֱמֹ֣ר לְבֵֽית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה לֹ֧א לְמַעַנְכֶ֛ם אֲנִ֥י עֹשֶׂ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל כִּ֤י אִם לְשֵׁם קָדְשִׁי֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר חִלַּלְתֶּ֔ם בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אתֶם שָֽׁם (oshb:Ezek.36.22) (“I don't do this for your sake” (web:Ezek.36.22)) opens with a 'therefore' consequence-clause: it draws out the result of the profanation narrated in the third person at Ezek.36.20 וַיָּב֗וֹא אֶל הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֣אוּ שָׁ֔ם וַֽיְחַלְּל֖וּ אֶת שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י בֶּאֱמֹ֤ר לָהֶם֙ עַם יְהוָ֣ה אֵ֔לֶּה וּמֵאַרְצ֖וֹ יָצָֽאוּ (oshb:Ezek.36.20) and Ezek.36.21 וָאֶחְמֹ֖ל עַל שֵׁ֣ם קָדְשִׁ֑י אֲשֶׁ֤ר חִלְּל֨וּהוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּגּוֹיִ֖ם אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אוּ שָֽׁמָּה (oshb:Ezek.36.21), where 'my holy name' is twice named as the thing profaned, and the same holy-name argument runs from there through 36.22 to the utterance close at 36.23. The turn from third-person narration to second-person address at 36.22 is disclosed here as a sub-onset within that one argument, not as an addressee change that would cut the unit. Close: the utterance formula at Ezek.36.23 וְקִדַּשְׁתִּ֞י אֶת שְׁמִ֣י הַגָּד֗וֹל הַֽמְחֻלָּל֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר חִלַּלְתֶּ֖ם בְּתוֹכָ֑ם וְיָדְע֨וּ הַגּוֹיִ֜ם כִּי אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה נְאֻם֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה בְּהִקָּדְשִׁ֥י בָכֶ֖ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Ezek.36.23), whose own bytes carry, immediately before the utterance formula, a recognition-pattern clause addressed to the nations (matching the recognition-family ‘know ... that I am Yahweh’ pattern directly visible in the full verse above). That clause is a member of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses book-wide) and refrain-grade in class; it and the utterance formula both stand mid-verse, with only a dependent temporal infinitive following them to the verse's end. The close's far face, 36.24, carries nothing of its own -- no particle, no onset class, no mark -- so the seam rests on this near face alone, and that is what this row's medium records.
P08-012.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through the gather/cleanse/new-heart material of 36.24-32 as one continuous salvation_oracle. Rejected because 36.23's recognition-plus-utterance material runs from the major disjunctive through to the verse's last word, its formula tokens standing mid-verse with only a dependent temporal infinitive (בְּהִקָּדְשִׁ֥י בָכֶ֖ם לְעֵינֵיהֶֽם, oshb:Ezek.36.23; WLC/OSHB, single witness) after them, which grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal and not the weak mid-verse shape, and 36.24 opens a fresh movement (the actual return and renewal) rather than continuing 36.16-23's retrospective argument about the profaned name, on its content and not on any particle of its own, since it carries none; splitting here keeps both resulting rows inside the 7-10 typical band.

P04-008.boundary_rationale: Every reference in this row touches MT ch 21 and is written dual. Onset: a strict word-event formula at web:Ezek.21.8 = oshb:Ezek.21.13 (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר), a hard seam, with a pe standing at the seam behind it, after web:Ezek.21.7 = oshb:Ezek.21.12 (single-witness), so that onset is two-faced. Close: the emphatic I-YHWH-have-spoken formula at web:Ezek.21.17 = oshb:Ezek.21.22 (וְגַם אֲנִ֗י אַכֶּ֤ה כַפִּי֙ אֶל כַּפִּ֔י וַהֲנִחֹתִ֖י חֲמָתִ֑י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבַּֽרְתִּי), with a pe immediately after. The poem's own refrains, sharpened and polished, the sword doubled and then tripled, run between the two; the one two-faced competing onset inside them, at web:Ezek.21.14 = oshb:Ezek.21.19, is weighed below and held as a paragraph. Both outer seams are top grade on both faces -- the word-event formula against the pe behind it, and the I-YHWH-have-spoken formula with its pe against the word-event formula at web:Ezek.21.18 = oshb:Ezek.21.23 past it -- and what holds this row at medium rather than high is that interior rival, which carries real evidence on both of its own faces.

P03-014.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:1 opens on the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.18.1); 18:2 quotes the popular proverb the oracle will refute, אָבוֹת֙ יֹ֣אכְלוּ בֹ֔סֶר וְשִׁנֵּ֥י הַבָּנִ֖ים תִּקְהֶֽינָה (oshb:Ezek.18.2) (“The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children’s teeth are set on edge”, web:Ezek.18.2). Close side: the span closes at 18:4, whose final clause הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֥יא תָמֽוּת (oshb:Ezek.18.4) ('the soul who sins shall die') states the disputation's thesis, and a samekh stands on this same verse in the single witness. An oath formula with the utterance signature stands at the head of 18:3, in that verse's first five words ('as I live, declares the Lord YHWH'), weighed as texture inside the refutation rather than a row-final close, since the clause on the proverb's future use runs on after it to the end of the same verse. The close at 18:4/18:5 is a case turn inside one word-event unit: 18:4 ends on the disputation's thesis and carries a samekh, 18:5 opens the righteous-man case with no formula of its own, and the samekh corroborates that turn without deciding it. A close seam of that shape is what this row's medium_low records. The onset seam, by contrast, is two-faced and top grade: 17:24 ends on the I-YHWH-have-spoken formula, verse-final, with a pe recorded after it, against 18:1's strict word-event formula.
P03-014.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 18:9 (thesis plus the first case-law example together) was weighed and not taken: the samekh on 18:4 corroborates a close for the thesis statement alone without deciding it, and 18:5 opens the righteous-man case with no formula of its own -- a fresh case argued on its own terms, rather than an illustration folded into the thesis that precedes it.

P03-015.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:5 opens with no formula device, the whole verse וְאִ֖ישׁ כִּי יִהְיֶ֣ה צַדִּ֑יק וְעָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּצְדָקָֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.5) ('if a man is righteous and does what is just and right'), a default case-law onset following the thesis stated at 18:4; the samekh recorded there, closing the unit before it, corroborates this row's onset from the far side of the seam. Close side: the row runs to 18:9, and its own final words are the utterance formula חָיֹ֣ה יִֽחְיֶ֔ה נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.9), a genuine verse-final refrain closing the first case before the wicked son's case opens at 18:10 with no formula of its own. That utterance is verse-final and carries no mark, and 18:10 brings no fresh onset past it, so it closes a paragraph inside the one word-event unit and not the unit itself; behind 18:5 the seam is a case turn with no formula on either face, corroborated by the samekh on 18:4 and not decided by it. Two seams of that shape are what this row's medium_low records.
P03-015.strongest_rejected_alternative: No parashah mark corroborates a seam at 18:9; keeping 18:5-9 fused with 18:10-20 into one eleven-plus-five-verse row was weighed and not taken because the utterance formula there is genuinely verse-final, unlike its four non-final recurrences elsewhere in MT 18 (18:3, 18:23, 18:30, 18:32).

P03-016.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:10 opens with no formula device, the whole verse וְהוֹלִ֥יד בֵּן פָּרִ֖יץ שֹׁפֵ֣ךְ דָּ֑ם וְעָ֣שָׂה אָ֔ח מֵאַחַ֖ד מֵאֵֽלֶּה (oshb:Ezek.18.10) ('and he fathers a violent son who sheds blood'), continuing the case-law series by default. The seam behind this onset is the one interior seam of the unit that carries a formula at all: 18:9 ends on the utterance signature, verse-final and unmarked, but 18:10 brings no fresh onset past it, so that signature is paragraph-final and not a unit close. The righteous grandson's case (18:14) and the summary restatement (18:19-20) follow without any fresh formula onset of their own, since 18:18 explicitly recalls the father's own guilt from 18:10-13 before drawing the general rule -- one continuous legal argument across three generations, not three independently onset units. Close side: the row runs through 18:20; its opening clause הַנֶּ֥פֶשׁ הַחֹטֵ֖את הִ֣יא תָמ֑וּת בֵּ֞ן לֹא יִשָּׂ֣א בַּעֲוֺ֣ן הָאָ֗ב (oshb:Ezek.18.20) ('the soul who sins shall die; a son shall not bear his father's iniquity') restates 18:4's thesis and closes the argument, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse. Both of this row's seams are case turns inside one word-event unit, with no formula on the near face of either: 18:21 opens the repentance case past the close with none of its own, and the samekh recorded on 18:20 corroborates that close without deciding it. Seams of that shape are what this row's medium_low records.

P03-017.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:21 opens with no formula device, וְהָרָשָׁ֗ע כִּ֤י יָשׁוּב֙ (oshb:Ezek.18.21) (“But if the wicked turns from all his sins that he has committed”, web:Ezek.18.21), a default onset for the repentance case; the running text reads the ketiv חטאתו (oshb:Ezek.18.21) in place of the pointed form. Close side: the row ends at 18:23, the whole verse הֶחָפֹ֤ץ אֶחְפֹּץ֙ מ֣וֹת רָשָׁ֔ע נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הֲל֛וֹא בְּשׁוּב֥וֹ מִדְּרָכָ֖יו וְחָיָֽה (oshb:Ezek.18.23), matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse. The utterance formula sits mid-verse there ('declares the Lord YHWH'), with the verse’s own final clause, “and not rather that he should return from his way, and live?” (web:Ezek.18.23), still to follow; the samekh stands on the whole verse regardless of the formula's mid-verse position, and it corroborates that close without deciding it: what the close rests on is the case turn itself, 18:23 ending the repentance case and 18:24 opening the reverse case with no formula of its own. Both of this row's seams are case turns of that shape inside one word-event unit -- no formula on either near face, a samekh corroborating and not deciding -- which is what this row's medium_low records.

P03-018.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:24 opens with no formula device, וּבְשׁ֨וּב צַדִּ֤יק מִצִּדְקָתוֹ֙ וְעָ֣שָׂה עָ֔וֶל (oshb:Ezek.18.24) (“But when the righteous turns away from his righteousness, and commits iniquity”, web:Ezek.18.24), the reverse case answering 18:21-23; the running text reads the ketiv צדקתו in place of the pointed form. Close side: 18:26 closes the row; its final clause בְּעַוְל֥וֹ אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂ֖ה יָמֽוּת (oshb:Ezek.18.26) ('for the injustice he has done he dies') restates the case's rule, matched by a samekh recorded on this same verse. Israel's objection is quoted between the case and its restatement, at 18:25, inside this same span. Both of this row's seams are case turns inside one word-event unit: no formula stands on either near face, 18:27 opens the positive case past the close with none of its own, and the samekh recorded on 18:23 behind the onset and on 18:26 at the close corroborates each turn without deciding it. Seams of that shape are what this row's medium_low records.

P03-019.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:27 opens with no formula device, וּבְשׁ֣וּב רָשָׁ֗ע מֵֽרִשְׁעָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.18.27) ('again, when a wicked person turns from the wickedness he has committed'), the positive repentance case answering 18:24-26; the running text reads the ketiv וישוב (oshb:Ezek.18.28) at 18:28. Israel's objection recurs at 18:29, a verse that carries a single-witness OSHB editorial note. The judgment proper then opens at 18:30 with לָכֵן֩ אִ֨ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֜יו אֶשְׁפֹּ֤ט אֶתְכֶם֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.18.30) (“Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, everyone according to his ways”, web:Ezek.18.30); the quoted run ends on the utterance formula, which stands mid-verse in 18:30 and is not itself the onset device. Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own end, 18:32, whose final clause וְהָשִׁ֖יבוּ וִֽחְיֽוּ (oshb:Ezek.18.32) ('so turn, and live') closes the chapter, matched by a pe recorded on this same verse; the utterance formula recurs mid-verse there rather than at the very end, so what carries this close is the chapter-final imperative clause, corroborated by the pe recorded on the verse and by the qinah command that opens at 19:1, a licensed onset on the far face. This row's onset, by contrast, is a case turn inside one word-event unit: 18:27 opens the positive case with no formula of its own, and the samekh recorded after 18:26 behind it corroborates the turn without deciding it. An onset seam of that shape is what this row's medium_low records, against a close that is two-faced.

P09-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: the verse opens on the hand-of-YHWH idiom immediately followed by a transport verb, oshb:Ezek.37.1 הָיְתָ֣ה עָלַי֮ יַד יְהוָה֒ וַיּוֹצִאֵ֤נִי בְר֨וּחַ֙ יְהוָ֔ה וַיְנִיחֵ֖נִי בְּת֣וֹךְ הַבִּקְעָ֑ה וְהִ֖יא מְלֵאָ֥ה עֲצָמֽוֹת -- the same onset shape that opens the book's other three long prose visions, and this occurrence is one of only 7 hand-of-YHWH verses in the book. The unit runs as one scene: the prophet is set down among the bones (37.1-2), questioned and commanded to prophesy twice -- once to the bones, once to the breath/spirit (37.4-6, 37.9), watches the two-stage reanimation (37.7-8, 37.10), and receives the scene's own interpretation as a word to 'son of man' (address.son_of_man, oshb:Ezek.37.11 וַיֹּאמֶר֮ אֵלַי֒ בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הָעֲצָמ֣וֹת הָאֵ֔לֶּה כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הֵ֑מָּה הִנֵּ֣ה אֹמְרִ֗ים יָבְשׁ֧וּ עַצְמוֹתֵ֛ינוּ וְאָבְדָ֥ה תִקְוָתֵ֖נוּ נִגְזַ֥רְנוּ לָֽנוּ). Close: oshb:Ezek.37.14 stacks three refrain-grade closes in one verse -- the second-person plural recognition variant ('and you will know that I am YHWH', part of a 21-verse 2mp family sweep), the emphatic 'I YHWH have spoken' close (one of 14 book-wide), and the short utterance signature without the divine-name pair (one of only 4 such short forms in the book) -- וְנָתַתִּ֨י רוּחִ֤י בָכֶם֙ וִחְיִיתֶ֔ם וְהִנַּחְתִּ֥י אֶתְכֶ֖ם עַל אַדְמַתְכֶ֑ם וִידַעְתֶּ֞ם כִּי אֲנִ֧י יְהוָ֛ה דִּבַּ֥רְתִּי וְעָשִׂ֖יתִי נְאֻם יְהוָֽה, and a pe mark is recorded immediately after this verse (tier-3 single-witness, informing not deciding). Both sides of the following seam were weighed: oshb:Ezek.37.15 opens with the strict word-event formula וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, one of 39 verses carrying that strict form, so the close at 37.14 and the fresh onset at 37.15 corroborate each other from both directions.
P09-001.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split at the two samekh-marked points inside the scene: after the army stands up at oshb:Ezek.37.10, and after the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.37.12 (tier-3 single-witness marks on both). The first is a real and licensed rival: 37.11 opens on a he-said-to-me clause with the son-of-man address (sweep: 93 verses book-wide), a default onset inside a vision, with the samekh standing behind it on 37.10 -- so 37.1-10 would be a complete scene (the question, the command to prophesy, and the army that stands up as its result) and 37.11-14 its interpretation, which carries a messenger formula of its own at 37.12 and a recognition close. It is not taken because 37.1-14 is one vision_report unit, opened by the hand-of-YHWH and transport at its head and closed by the formula stack at 37.14; the other he-said-to-me verses inside the scene (37.3, 37.4, 37.9) are dialogue turns that leave no scene-complete piece behind them, and the transport at 37.2 would leave a one-verse remainder. That licensed rival is what holds this row at medium rather than high; which of the recognition clauses at 37.6, 37.13 and 37.14 closes the row is held open here.
P09-001.device_notes: 37.2 and 37.9 each carry one paseq (count-only, single-witness, no intra-verse position sourceable from the extract). 37.9 also carries an OSHB editorial note recording an accent divergence from BHS (single-witness apparatus, not a text variant). The WEB prints a mid-verse paragraph inside 37.3 (“Son of man, can these bones live?” (web:Ezek.37.3), then the prophet's reply) -- tier-4 texture, cited only and never a boundary argument. The witness also records a samekh after MT 36:38 (single witness), the paragraph mark behind this row's onset. A second-person-plural recognition formula stands at 37.6, interior to the scene (sweep: 21 verses book-wide).

P09-010.boundary_rationale: Onset: no word-event, messenger, hand-of-YHWH or address formula opens 39:21, whose near face therefore carries no device of any tracked class, and no mark stands at 39:20 either; the seam rests on the verse-final utterance signature at 39:20 alone, together with the topical turn from the birds-and-beasts summons to a first-person retrospective on Israel's exile. Inside that retrospective the wide-family recognition close addressed to “the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.39.22) stands at 39.22, one of the expansions in the 64-verse wide sweep and not the strict 28, and is internal, paragraph-final rather than row-final; 39.23 is no second such close -- its knowing-clause carries no divine-name predicate and belongs to no tracked class. An onset whose near face carries no device at all is what this row's low grade records. Close: 39.21-24 ends at oshb:Ezek.39.24 כְּטֻמְאָתָ֥ם וּכְפִשְׁעֵיהֶ֖ם עָשִׂ֣יתִי אֹתָ֑ם וָאַסְתִּ֥ר פָּנַ֖י מֵהֶֽם, with a samekh mark recorded immediately after (tier-3 single-witness); 39.25 then reopens with a fresh messenger formula, weighed from the far side of the seam.

P02-008.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.1 וַתִּשָּׂ֨א אֹתִ֜י ר֗וּחַ וַתָּבֵ֣א אֹ֠תִי אֶל שַׁ֨עַר בֵּית יְהוָ֤ה הַקַּדְמוֹנִי֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ימָה וְהִנֵּה֙ בְּפֶ֣תַח הַשַּׁ֔עַר עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ וָאֶרְאֶ֨ה בְתוֹכָ֜ם אֶת יַאֲזַנְיָ֧ה בֶן עַזֻּ֛ר וְאֶת פְּלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן בְּנָיָ֖הוּ שָׂרֵ֖י הָעָֽם — a fresh transport (“the Spirit lifted me up and brought me” (web:Ezek.11.1)) to the east gate, introducing new participants (Jaazaniah son of Azzur, Pelatiah son of Benaiah). A pe follows this very verse (single-witness): it is a mid-row mark, standing after 11:1 and inside the row, disclosed and not cut, as the pe after 11:6 is. The onset itself rests on the transport at 11:1, a predicate-class member carrying two tokens, while the far face behind it, 10:22, carries no mark and no formula -- chapter 10 carries no parashah mark at all in this witness. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.13 וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּהִנָּ֣בְאִ֔י וּפְלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן בְּנָיָ֖ה מֵ֑ת וָאֶפֹּ֨ל עַל פָּנַ֜י וָאֶזְעַ֣ק קוֹל גָּד֗וֹל וָאֹמַר֙ אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה כָּלָה֙ אַתָּ֣ה עֹשֶׂ֔ה אֵ֖ת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל — Pelatiah's death and the prophet's cry “Ah Lord Yahweh! Will you make a full end of the remnant of Israel?” (web:Ezek.11.13) — is a narrative close; a pe follows this verse as well (single-witness), and that mark is this close seam's corroboration. Both sides: the courtyard scene runs as one continuous unit from the transport to the prophet's cry, with a sub-onset at oshb:Ezek.11.5 “Yahweh's Spirit fell on me, and he said to me, 'Speak …” (web:Ezek.11.5) that introduces direct judgment speech but carries no word-event formula and is not itself an addressee-class shift, so it is disclosed as internal texture rather than a competing row seam. Both near faces are licensed -- the transport at 11:1, the narrative close at 11:13 with its pe -- while the onset's far face is bare, and that is what this row's medium records.
